_README: Every declaration whose `#print axioms` line mentions Classical.choice, and
Coverage is by exhaustive sweep, not by the hand-written `#print axioms`
lines: audit.py generates a print for every declaration the parser can see.
Five Phase 1 results were classical and unaudited until it did -- a check that
only sees what someone remembered to print is not a check.
what justifies it. `tools/audit.py` fails if this file and the build disagree
in either direction, so a new classical result cannot land unexamined and a
stale entry cannot outlive its subject.
An audit line is an upper bound: it says a proof used choice, not that the
theorem needs it. FINDINGS 24 is that gap caught in the act -- `cut_located`
and `located_bracket` are the same walk, and only one pays. So `reversed` is
the only status that establishes anything:
reversed   -- Reverse.lean proves, choice-free, that the statement implies
EM (or the weaker principle named). The dependency is real.
definition -- a def rather than a proposition; nothing to reverse.
inherited  -- classical only through something else it is stated over. Not
known to be essential; `note` says where the constructive
content lives.
open       -- classical, and no reversal found. Counted against
_open_budget, which ratchets: a new one fails the build, and
clearing one requires lowering the budget to lock it in.
There is no `accepted` status on purpose. If a result is genuinely classical
it can be reversed; if it cannot be, it is not yet understood -- and `open`
says exactly that instead of pretending otherwise.
axiom      -- a declared axiom of Phase 1. It is the subject of the audit,
not a result to be justified against it.
equivalent -- both directions: the statement implies the principle, and the
principle proves the statement, each choice-free. This pins the
result to exactly that strength, which a Phase 2 audit line
cannot do on its own -- Lean derives em from choice and reports
only choice.

_equivalences.note: the step that turns 'no sequence is known to leave the tree' into an actual path. Reverses to LLPO ALONE, with no compactness and no FAN -- the reversal's tree stays alive by a decidable bounded search (analysis FINDINGS 748), so the selection carries the entire strength of the fan-to-Koenig gap. A LOWER BOUND ONLY: no forward is proved. Moved here from _unplaced once the witness was in this tree (DECISIONS 657)

weak Koenig's lemma yields LLPO, over the same detachable List Bool trees FAN uses. A LOWER BOUND ONLY: no forward is proved, so this is not an equivalence and must not be read as one. Whether WKL -> LPO, or WKL sits strictly between LLPO and LPO in this encoding, is open (FINDINGS 746)

deciding equivalence of two ideals of a non-trivial ring. The reversal is choice-free and needs no integral closure, trace form or invertibility, and it is instantiated at Z[zeta_p] itself by em_of_cyc_idealEquiv_decidable. The forward direction is one line and is kept BECAUSE it is the non-vacuity witness: a reversal whose hypothesis is unsatisfiable measures nothing

deciding 0's membership in the lower cut of a real built by the ternary walk. For an arbitrary cut the same decision is EM (FINDINGS 20); restricted to a real named by a binary sequence it is exactly LPO
deciding whether a walk-built real *is* zero. One quantifier weaker than membership in its cut, and correspondingly one step down the lattice from LPO
a walk-built real that is not zero has a digit. This is Markov's principle transported across the walk, and it is the step from TernaryZeroDecidable's Pi statement to TernaryDecidable's Sigma one
of two walk-built reals that cannot both be positive, one is at most zero. The analytic form of LLPO, and the fourth mark now occupied on the ruler
comparability of von Neumann ordinals. Both directions now proved, so the first ordinal entry is pinned rather than one-sided (FINDINGS 33)
an inhabited set of ordinals has a least member. The reversal runs on the two-element set {empty, propOrd p}, where being least forces empty and comparing decides p
every subset of a finite set is finite. Both directions now: deciding how many elements {z in 1 | p} has decides p, and em supplies the detachability that isFinite_of_detachable needs (FINDINGS 57)
a uniformly continuous function on [0,1] attains its mean value. Reverses to LLPO alone; the forward needs BinaryDC and DC as well, so the gap is exactly two named choice layers (FINDINGS 730, 736)

a uniform derivative takes every intermediate value. Same bounds as the mean-value shape through a different machine -- the content is that a uniform derivative is uniformly continuous, so the C1 bundle's continuity field is derivable rather than assumed (FINDINGS 731, 737) Those bounds are BinaryDC and DC, named here rather than left to the reference: llpo is the floor, not the value.

an exact zero-crossing, as against the approximate one which is free. The first of the four sandwiches closed, and the one that fixed the shape (FINDINGS 732, 733-734) BRACKETED, NOT PINNED: the reversal yields llpo; the forward's type also takes DC and BinaryDC, so llpo is the floor.

a uniformly continuous function on [0,1] attains its maximum -- the exact half of the extreme value theorem, whose approximate half is free. The reversal is proved; the converse climb is the analysis track's open item, so this end of the sandwich is not yet witnessed (FINDINGS 735) A forward IS witnessed, but only with two principles more than the reversal yields: maxAttainment_of_llpo_binaryDC_dc takes LLPO, BinaryDC and DC, so the entry is BRACKETED rather than pinned. The climb at LLPO alone -- the pinning FINDINGS 735 is after -- remains open.

naming the order of a power series -- the least index whose coefficient survives -- given a vanishing readout. Both directions are proved and `exists_ord_iff` bundles them, so this is an EQUIVALENCE and not a bound. The polynomial mirror, `exists_deg_iff`, prices the same question at DecidableVanishing with no omniscience at all: the support bound turns an unbounded search into a bounded scan, and that is the whole of the gap (FINDINGS 774)

a located real distinct from zero is apart from it -- the positive cone's `total` clause for RealL, and the same principle the geometry track reached independently (FINDINGS 788). BRACKETED, NOT PINNED: mp_of_neApartZero gives MP and is choice-free; neApartZero_of_mp_of_locators returns it from MP PLUS HasZeroLocators. The gap is therefore INSIDE THE LOCATORS, not in countable choice -- the earlier ceiling took CountableBoolChoice and spent it only on manufacturing a locator, which is the inherited-premise shape and was caught by geometry (FINDINGS 789). Whether locators give countable choice back is an independence this development declines to settle (DECISIONS 797), so read `mp` as the FLOOR. Reading a firing digit back off an apartness costs nothing (FINDINGS 784), and LPO's extra strength over MP buys the DECISION rather than the witness (FINDINGS 785). The cut encoding's same clause needs realNonneg_or, which reverses to em, so the two encodings' orders sit at different lattice points (FINDINGS 782)

a finite set has 2^n subsets. Reverses to EM at n = 1 ALONE: the subsets of a one-point set are the propositions, so counting them decides them -- and for an ARBITRARY proposition, not a decidable one, which is why this lands at em rather than anywhere in the omniscience lattice. NOW AN EQUIVALENCE: `powersetCount_of_em` supplies the forward (structures), and `em` enters it at EXACTLY ONE place -- discharging the detachability hypothesis of `exists_subsetOf_eq` for an arbitrary subset -- which is precisely the step the reversal proves cannot be avoided, so the two halves meet at the same point from opposite sides. It stays a HYPOTHESIS there, so no audit line moves and the choice budget is untouched. The file had asserted this equivalence for its whole life while proving one direction. Written because Hall's theorem wanted to search subsets and the powerset looked like the object; `subsetOf` is the constructive replacement, indexing the DETACHABLE subsets by a bitmask over an enumeration

an unbounded monochromatic set for a detachable symmetric colouring of pairs. Reverses to LPO: join i and j when the sequence is true somewhere at or below min i j, and an unbounded monochromatic set decides it -- two joined points witness a true, while for each n two unjoined points above n force the value false there. A LOWER BOUND ONLY; whether LPO plus DC suffices is open and the upper bound is expected to want DC as a hypothesis, as Baire does. THE POINT OF THE PAIR: the FINITE theorem (ZFSet.ramsey) is free under the SAME hypotheses -- Bool-valued colouring, symmetric -- so the two differ only in the size of the carrier and the gap between them is a principle rather than a proof technique (FINDINGS 5023)

_equivalences.landmark: the infinite pigeonhole for two colours
_equivalences.note: one of two values occurs unboundedly often in a Bool sequence -- step 2 of infinite Ramsey's nested-subset construction, NAMED so it can be measured instead of buried in the theorem. BOTH DIRECTIONS: reverses to LPO through the RUNNING OR, and holds under em. The reversal is the finding: a quantifier-complexity argument said Pi-2 unboundedness could not follow from Sigma-1 LPO, and predicted a gap TWICE. It was correct about the complexity and irrelevant, because monotonising is a CONSTRUCTION and the reversal never decides anything -- for a monotone sequence the branches stop being symmetric, true-unboundedly-often collapsing to true-somewhere and false-unboundedly-often forcing false-everywhere. `runningOr` depends on no axioms at all

a uniformly differentiable function agreeing at the endpoints has an interior point of vanishing derivative. Reverses through the SAME median gadget as Darboux, shifted by its own mean so the integral over [0,1] vanishes and F 0 = F 1 is SUPPLIED by the construction rather than assumed; the interior zero is then the identical attainment equation signDisjunction_of_darboux obtains, so the two reversals share their closing step. Ceiling rolle01_of_llpo_binaryDC_dc; both directions [propext, Quot.sound] (FINDINGS 984)

DECIDING whether 1/(x+t) is uniformly continuous on [0,1], for t the ternary real of a bit sequence, is exactly WLPO. The hypothesis must be the decision and not the assertion: the assertion is REFUTABLE at the all-zero sequence (not_uniformlyContinuousOn_ivtSpike_of_eq_zero), so an implication out of it would be vacuous. Forward direction uniformlyContinuousOn_ivtSpike prices it at an apartness; both directions [propext, Quot.sound] (FINDINGS 1002)

deciding whether two circles meet in ONE point or TWO. BOTH DIRECTIONS, both [propext, Quot.sound]. THE POINT OF THE PAIR: Euclid I.1 itself is FREE (sqDist_meet_equilateral) because it never asks which of the two points it got -- it asserts a distance, and both intersection points satisfy it. The brief predicted circle-circle intersection would land on a lattice node and aimed it one theorem too early (FINDINGS 3178). It lands here, at the question that TELLS THE TWO POINTS APART. Quantified over Nat -> Bool rather than over an arbitrary radius, which is load-bearing: over arbitrary located reals the reversal still gives WLPO but the forward direction does not return, because located yields a disjunction and turning one into WLPO's bit is defining data by cases (ternary_vanishing_of_wlpo). So a Prop over arbitrary radii would be a BOUND and not a node (FINDINGS 3185)

DECIDING EQUALITY OF SETS IS EXACTLY EXCLUDED MIDDLE. Both directions choice-free, the forward at NO AXIOMS AT ALL. The reversal is one separation: sep (fun _ => P) (singleton empty) equals singleton empty exactly when P holds, so a decision procedure reads P off a comparison -- compared against the SINGLETON rather than empty, because the other reading needs a witness out of a non-empty set, the step regularity pays Classical.choice for (FINDINGS 1026)

AND DECIDING MEMBERSHIP IS TOO, with a shorter witness: empty in sep (fun _ => P) (singleton empty) IS P, so separation alone carries it and no extensionality step appears. This is the one actually tempting to assume -- decidable membership reads as a convenience where decidable equality looks like a strong hypothesis, and both are the whole of em. Together they are why condP exists and why every definition-by-cases in the tower is built by separation rather than by branching (FINDINGS 1026)

DECIDING RATIONAL ORDER AS A PROP-LEVEL DECISION reverses to WEM, though rational order is perfectly decidable mathematically and ratLt_or_not proves exactly that free. Witness: condP P ratOne ratZero is a rational reading ratOne when P holds and ratZero when it fails, so comparing it against ratZero reads P back. WEM and NOT EM, and the asymmetry is the content -- the negative branch gives not-P outright, the positive gives only not-not-P, because ratZero < X does not say WHICH value X took. A BRACKET, NOT AN EQUIVALENCE: decidableRatLt_of_em gives the upper bound EM, WEM and EM are distinct, and no forward from WEM is proved, so the bracket does not close. Note also that this hypothesis PRICES the merge without being able to PERFORM it -- Or lives in Prop, so Or.casesOn cannot eliminate into Type and no count can be built from it (FINDINGS 1026, item 1031)

deciding membership in a half-open interval of located reals for an ARBITRARY set, and it is EQUIVALENT to excluded middle -- both directions named, so this is a measurement rather than a bound. Registered here because the strength arrives as a HYPOTHESIS and not as an axiom, so audit.py cannot see it: lebesgueOuter_unionUpto_dyadic assumes it, which makes the dyadic subdivision classical as stated even though every accumulation step around it is free. The contrast is the content: CutAtRat is the SAME comparison for a w already supplied with a rational bracket, is free, and is what dyadicPiece_covers uses -- so the gap between the two readings is the whole of EM and lies entirely in the quantifier's range (analysis FINDINGS 1199).

deciding whether two objects of a DISCRETE category are isomorphic. An equivalence, both directions choice-free, and the category track's opening measurement. The interest is not the number but WHERE it sits: composition in a category is partial and its guard is a ZFSet equality in every clause, so that guard is where a cost was expected -- and it costs nothing, since the guard is a hypothesis and even the TOTAL composition discComp is free (isCategory_disc, propext and Quot.sound only). What costs is the first question the subject asks about two objects. Stated at a FAMILY parameterised by a Bool sequence, which is what buys the equivalence: the general form, deciding isomorphism in an ARBITRARY category, is an upper bound at em with no reversal available, and writing that down instead would have recorded a bound where an equivalence exists. TernaryZeroDecidable is the identical construction at the reals

deciding whether two objects of the CATEGORY OF SETS are isomorphic, where isomorphism is a bijection rather than equality of objects. Both directions choice-free, so this is an equivalence and not a bound. THE CARRIER IS DEGENERATE AND THE ENTRY MUST SAY SO, because the entry is what gets read as the measurement: W is pair empty (fireSet a), so one object is empty and a set equinumerous with empty IS empty, which makes a bijection carry no more information than an equality. Landing on the same node as DiscIsoDecidable is therefore an artefact of the carrier and is NOT evidence that the two questions have equal strength -- in the discrete category a single arrow settles isomorphism and the inverse is never examined, while here both composites are consumed, which is the structural reason to expect them to differ somewhere. Where they differ is not reached here and the obvious guess is refuted: comparing two UNBOUNDED detachable subsets of omega measures nothing, since any two are provably equinumerous by enumUp. The live question is Equinumerous omega x, which for detachable x is Cofinal x -- the sequence firing infinitely often -- a Pi-2 statement this lattice has no node for.

two distinct points of the plane are APART -- the incidence geometry's reading of the same gap `NeApartZero` prices on the line. INTER-DERIVABLE WITH `NeApartZero`, both directions named and both choice-free: `ZFSet.distinctApart_of_neApart` and `ZFSet.neApart_of_distinctApart`. A LOWER BOUND ONLY, and deliberately: `distinctApart_of_mp` does not exist, so the forward can only be reached through `NeApartZero`'s, which is itself bracketed by `HasZeroLocators` -- composing two brackets is not a pinning and the entry must not read as one. REGISTERED BECAUSE ITS ABSENCE COST A DUPLICATED PROOF: structures searched `Reverse.lean` and both registries for *does DistinctApart reverse to MP*, found nothing, proved it, and then found `neApart_of_distinctApart` already here. Reversals do not all live in `Reverse.lean` -- this one sits beside the definition it prices, which is the better place -- so the search was reasonable and the conclusion was not available from it. A registry that does not name a statement is not evidence the statement is unmeasured; it is evidence about the REGISTRY. THE BRIDGE IS GEOMETRY'S AND IS WORTH KEEPING: splitting on WHICH coordinate differs would be weak excluded middle, so the proof goes through the SQUARED DISTANCE -- a single real -- and comes back by cotransitivity, turning one apartness into two without deciding which. That is why the two-dimensional form costs nothing over the one-dimensional one. GEOMETRY PROPOSED A `forward` FIELD AND IT IS NOT ONE: `distinctApart_of_neApart` derives this from `NeApartZero`, not from the landmark principle, and there is no derivation of either from `mp` in the tree -- the reverse direction is `mp_of_neApartZero`, which points the other way -- so the chain is DistinctApart <-> NeApartZero -> mp with no return, which is a lower bound and not a pinning.

_equivalences.landmark: ideal theory over a Dedekind domain
_equivalences.note: deciding whether an ARBITRARY ideal sits inside a given MAXIMAL one, which is `exists_idealProdList_eq_of_primeProductList`'s `hsubP`. Tested at `propIdealOf R zero p`, whose membership is `p` away from zero: containment forces not-p since a maximal ideal is proper, and a witness outside forces p since zero is inside. Needs ONE maximal ideal to test against, so it is stated with M supplied rather than quantified. A LOWER BOUND ONLY: no forward is proved, though em plainly gives it. THE POINT: the same lemma's `ACC` reverses only to LPO, so pricing that route from `ACC` alone understates it by a full lattice node -- a signature's cost is its WORST binder, not its first informative one (DECISIONS 12275's correction)

deciding whether the EQUALIZER of a parallel pair is INITIAL, in the category of sets over a fired carrier. Both directions choice-free, so an equivalence rather than a bound. Same lattice node as SetCatIsoDecidable and by the same underlying mechanism -- both collapse to whether fireSet is empty -- but reached through a different UNIVERSAL PROPERTY, which is what makes it a third point on the control rather than a restatement of the second. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS ENTRY WRONG: if the equalizer's initiality were decidable at a carrier where fireSet is NOT the deciding factor, the note's mechanism claim fails even though the two theorems stand

deciding, for an ARBITRARY set E, whether opair i j is in it, for i and j ranging over omega. An equivalence: both directions are choice-free [propext, Quot.sound]. REGISTERED BECAUSE THE HYPOTHESIS IS EVERYWHERE AND WAS UNPRICED -- DetachablePairs appears seventeen times across RamseySet, RamseyRel and RamseyMerge and is a hypothesis at every one, which is what keeps those theorems constructive; nothing named its unrestricted form or measured it, so analysis was right to flag it and the grep for *_of_detachablePairs came back empty. THE ENTRY IS ABOUT THE CLOSURE, NOT THE USES: DetachablePairs E for a single E is not classical and must not be read as such. THE WITNESS NEEDS ONE PAIR: sep (fun _ => P) (singleton (opair 0 0)) contains opair 0 0 exactly when P, so the decision at i = j = 0 alone gives P or not P -- the quantifier over omega is never used. So this does not merely inherit from DecidableMemSet being classical (em_of_decidableMemSet): that decides EVERY membership, while this decides only memberships of ordered pairs of naturals, a strictly narrower family, and it is already all of excluded middle

dne: reversed by `em_of_dne`. Pinned: Phase 1. Equivalent to em, not weaker
byContradiction: reversed by `em_of_byContradiction`. Pinned: Phase 1. dne under another name
byCases: reversed by `em_of_dne`. Pinned: Phase 1. Case analysis on an arbitrary proposition -- em applied
peirce: reversed by `em_of_peirce`. Pinned: Phase 1. Reverses with b := False
contrapose': reversed by `em_of_contrapose'`. Pinned: Phase 1. dne in disguise
not_and_or: reversed by `wem_of_not_and_or`. Pinned: Phase 1. De Morgan's third law -- weak excluded middle, not em. Same split as sdiff_inter one phase later (FINDINGS 4)
imp_iff_not_or: reversed by `em_of_imp_iff_not_or`. Pinned: Phase 1. Reverses at a := b
exists_not_of_not_forall: reversed by `wem_of_exists_not_of_not_forall`. Phase 1. Reverses to WEM, not em: the witness lands on Not a or on Not (Not a), and the second is where em would be needed. The earlier attempts failed because they aimed at em
drinker: reversed by `wem_of_drinker`. Phase 1. Same two-element family as exists_not_of_not_forall, same WEM
Exists.witness: reversed by `choice_of_witness`. Phase 1. Together with witness_spec it reconstructs the axiom, so it is choice rather than a consequence of it
Exists.witness_spec: reversed by `choice_of_witness`. Phase 1. The property half of the same reconstruction
em: Phase 1 declares it. The thing under audit, not a consequence of it
choice: Phase 1 declares it. Reconstructed by choice_of_witness, so Exists.witness is exactly this
decider_of_em: reversed by `em_of_decider`. Phase 1. The gap between proving by cases and defining by cases, measured: em is a hypothesis here, not an axiom, so [choice] is what turning Or p (Not p) into data costs. em_of_decider is the axiom-free converse. Phase 2's realMul, dcNum and dcDigit all sit on this (FINDINGS 163)

_families.name: the ternary walk
_families.carrier: a real named by a binary sequence, `nestLower (tlowSeq (boolDigit a))`
_families.varied: the LOGICAL FORM of the question
_families.result: four forms, four different lattice points -- lpo, wlpo, mp, llpo. Deciding a membership is Sigma and costs LPO; deciding an equality is Pi and costs WLPO; the implication between them is MP; the two-sequence form is LLPO.
_families.note: THE VARYING FAMILY. This is the only place the price moves while the object stays put.

_families.name: exact existence on the unit interval
_families.carrier: a uniformly continuous function on [0,1], located reals
_families.held_fixed: the logical form -- each is `exists c in [0,1]` with an EXACT condition at c
_families.varied: the mathematical content: maximum, mean value, zero crossing, intermediate derivative
_families.result: four contents, ONE lattice point -- llpo for all four.
_families.note: THE CONTROL, and the one that makes the ternary family mean something: it varies the other variable and the price does not move.

_families.name: selection from a binary tree
_families.held_fixed: carrier and form -- both produce a path from a non-emptiness
_families.varied: the hypothesis: not dying out, versus being infinite
_families.result: both llpo, and both converses open.
_families.note: A second control, weaker than the first because only two questions are asked.

_families.name: von Neumann ordinals
_families.varied: comparability of two, versus a least element of a set
_families.result: both em, both pinned in both directions.
_families.note: The third control, and the only family sitting at `em` rather than inside the omniscience lattice.

_contrasts.name: Baire, finite against omega-indexed
_contrasts.carrier: a family of dense open subsets of `RealL`, refined by the same shrinking step
_contrasts.held_fixed: carrier, file, and the refinement step itself
_contrasts.varied: whether the iteration is FINITE or omega-indexed

members.note: choice-free: finitely many refinements need no principle to iterate

DC is taken as a HYPOTHESIS and is an upper bound, not a measurement. Baire.lean:450 argues the gap is not merely unmeasured: a reversal here can only produce dependent choice for relations on a set embedding in the reals -- `DCOmega` -- and no argument from Baire reaches full `DC`, which quantifies over every set.

_contrasts.result: the whole cost of the category theorem on this carrier is the ITERATION, not the topology: the refinement step is the same term in both and is free.
